site_name: 1 Redheughs Avenue (former RBS headquarters / Drummond House site)

max_building_height_m.claimant: Shelborn Drummond Ltd / studioNWA Architects (illustrative height parameter at PPP stage)
max_building_height_m.notes: 25-32 m parameter for the illustrative design, allowing 2 to 2.5 floors of data halls above ground-level electrical infrastructure rooms; prior extant office consent (22/05659/FUL) included six blocks exceeding 33 m. Final heights would be set at MSC/detailed stage.

number_of_buildings.notes: Two separate data centre buildings plus dedicated electrical substation, enclosed standby generator compounds, security lodge and parking.

current_land_use: Cleared former office site (Drummond House, former RBS headquarters built 1993, demolished c. 2022) with the retained Younger Building, hardstanding car parking and a central landscaped green space protected by City Plan 2030 Policy Env 23
previous_land_use: Royal Bank of Scotland headquarters campus (offices)

nearest_home_distance_m.notes: Refers to a consented mixed-use development including housing about 50 m from the data centre site, expected to start construction in 2026 (Parabola/Edinburgh Park scheme), not existing occupied homes. APRS also stated the site is 220 m from a nursery and close to residential homes.

protected_designations: On-site protected open space (City Plan 2030 Policy Env 23) - proposed to be relocated as a new public park fronting Lochside Court
land_notes: Urban business-park site bounded by Redheughs Avenue to the north and South Gyle Crescent to the south-east, within the Edinburgh Park/South Gyle 'Place 19' area of City Plan 2030 (strategic business centre with an intended shift to a wider mix of uses including housing). Extant planning permission for a Class 4 office development with mobility hub and ancillary uses (22/05659/FUL, granted January 2024) which the applicant elected not to build out. DPEA case GIS reference: Eastings 318354, Northings 671837, consistent with the coordinates above. Boundary polygon not digitised: PAN red line drawing seen only as a low-resolution consultation-board image, so no defensible geojson could be produced.
